items.title: Rain damage hits Mustang as tourism and harvest season begins
items.blurb: Landslides and river erosion have disrupted the main road, while power and internet outages are hitting tourism, apple farmers and local trade.

items.title: Flood cuts off market access for Rasuwa farmers as vegetables pile up
items.blurb: Farmers in Gatlang had expanded cultivation after strong returns last year, but damaged roads and bridges now threaten to leave this year’s harvest rotting in the fields.

items.title: Flood-hit districts remain cut off from national road network
items.blurb: Repairs are underway in Manang, Mustang, Baglung and Rasuwa, but damaged bridges and approach roads continue to disrupt direct road links.

items.title: Nepal’s growth to slow to 3.7 percent after devastating Rasuwa flood
items.blurb: The World Bank estimates $1.66 billion in direct damage to physical assets, with infrastructure accounting for 83 percent of the losses.

items.title: 34 blackbucks die; 20 go missing in 15 months
items.blurb: The population in the Khairapur conservation area has fallen to 210, with leopard attacks accounting for the most deaths.

items.title: Nepal’s disaster panel is debating what to call the Bhotekoshi floods. ‘Himalayan tsunami’ isn’t on the list
items.blurb: Prime Minister Balendra Shah used the term at the UN, but experts on the government panel say they are considering other names for the August 26 disaster.
